review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 24, 6:55 PM ET. It had Golden Flashes 36% and Eagles 64%, projecting Golden Flashes 19.7 – Eagles 25.3 (45 total, Eagles by 5.6).

Final: Golden Flashes 12 – Eagles 17. Right winner: it had Eagles at 64%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Golden Flashes came in with a 35% below average attack and a 41% leakier than average defense (3-8, 14.5 scored and 29.8 allowed a game over 11 games), worth about 37 and 180 games of evidence. Projected to score 19.7, they scored 12 (−7.7 points, 39% under); projected to allow 25.3, they allowed 17 (−8.3 points, 33% under).

Eagles came in with a 30% below average attack and a 29% leakier than average defense (4-7, 20.5 scored and 27.3 allowed a game over 11 games), worth about 183 and 182 games of evidence. Projected to score 25.3, they scored 17 (−8.3 points, 33% under); projected to allow 19.7, they allowed 12 (−7.7 points, 39% under).

The bigger miss was Eagles' scoring (-8.3 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 29 against 45 projected (-16), about the 15th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±15.5).

Margin: Eagles by 5 against Eagles by 5.6 projected, about the 48th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±15.3).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.610 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by -1.2 points. It counts toward CFB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 201 graded CFB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.940 and gives home teams -0.6 points. Team corrections so far: Golden Flashes attack ×0.960, defense ×0.985 (3 games); Eagles attack ×0.960, defense ×1.012 (3 games).
